success_patterns: Read parameter and domain quantifiers literally: distinguish constants allowed to depend on ε, uniform claims for every parameter value from eventual claims, and exact endpoint or range conditions.
Compare the full logical structure of nearby choices: equivalence versus one-way implication, equality versus inclusion, and every term and index in an exact identity.
Assess extra clauses independently of the main conclusion, including uniqueness, regularity, algorithms, and whether a claim covers the whole object or only one component.

patch.reasoning: The current skill already captures quantifier scope, logical strength, regularity, and exact formula comparison, so those patterns need no redundant edits. A useful refinement is to distinguish algorithmic decision from witness construction and to check all components when an identity is justified by a decomposition.

edits.content:
- For algorithmic claims, distinguish deciding whether a condition holds from constructing explicit witnesses; neither capability follows merely from existence or an equivalence.
- When an identity is presented through a decomposition into components, verify the transformation or cancellation of every component, including exceptional terms. Invariance of one component alone does not establish invariance of the whole expression.
